ticket.title: Attention v34: only real asks count, a human's reply clears, every waiting item is reachable, drop the rail "Waiting on you" entry and the comment dot, Dismiss, stale cleanup
ticket.description:
Owner rulings m-8aa6439a77 on m-14333c915c, design-e963c656f5 v34 §4.18. Measured: the owner's list had 21 items on the epic, 18 of them FYI statuses from the architect; the epic page highlighted only 3, and the rest could not be found.
1. **attention.py / board.inbox:** an item counts only if it is a question or steer, a status with status in blocked/failed/deferred, or a deviation to a human. A plain status, note or finding never counts (narrows t-9e9ba3a6e5).
2. **Clearing:** any later message from the human on the same ticket, addressed to the asker or with reply_to set to the ask, resolves it. Case: the owner answered the S8 ask m-584a1c342d with m-f5f30e92bb (to the engineer, no reply_to), and it stayed highlighted.
3. **Reachability:** the Conversation loads back to the oldest waiting message, or shows an "N earlier waiting" bar at the thread top whose items load and scroll to each one. The Work drawer's ticket highlight must lead to the message on the ticket page.
4. **Remove** the rail "Waiting on you" entry and its AnchoredPanel (AppShell), and update the notification fallback copy that names it.
5. **In-thread marker:** keep the large highlight. Remove the AttentionDot from the comment, and restyle the tag as the quiet caption used for "For your information".
6. **Dismiss:** per item (a server-side dismissal, so it clears everywhere), plus "Dismiss all updates" on the epic.
7. **One-off cleanup:** a script, or a migration, that resolves the pre-v34 items the new rule no longer counts. Report before/after counts for the owner.
8. **Markdown:** the message renderer accepts a GFM table that starts right after a paragraph line; fixture m-14333c915c must render as a table.
Tests: pytest (rule, clearing, dismiss, cleanup), vitest (panels, marker), and ONE Playwright spec (s20-attention) run alone with ≥1.5 GB free RAM. Rebuild the SPA from PowerShell; the architect deploys. No consult.

tickets.words: Today the app is hardcoded to run on my machine. I would like it to be run on anyone's machine with a proper installer and need to publish this on Git as a distributable.
